src.label: The 5 Best Songs Of The Week, Oct 16

items.title: Fresh Start
items.note: An 85-second grungy pop-punk track with riffs, tangled guitar work, and hooky vocals; the writer compares its emo-as-power-pop sound to Oso Oso.

src.label: The 5 Best Songs Of The Week, Oct 16

items.title: i think he's got a girl
items.note: Follows her album WOR$T GIRL IN AMERICA with slanted, hazy, rock-infused pop that the writer calls infectious and cinematic.

src.label: The 5 Best Songs Of The Week, Oct 23

items.title: Ringtone
items.note: A catchy, charming 2000s-style love song about ringtones, blending elegant and chintzy sounds around a hook about God, love, and world peace.

src.label: The 5 Best Songs Of The Week, Oct 23

items.title: Little Things
items.note: A bright single that reminds listeners of the world outside their heads, with galloping drums, synth bloops, and a feeling that everyday things are magic.

src.label: The 5 Best Songs Of The Week, Oct 23

items.title: Circadian Heart
items.note: Hannah Frances says it's about choosing unavailable people and trying to get them to choose her back; it moves between folk sprawls and jazzy ascensions.

src.label: The 5 Best Songs Of The Week, Oct 23

items.title: White Flag
items.note: A hammer-skitter lo-fi electroclash track that contrasts with Dido's song of the same name, embracing surrender as a warlike tantrum.

src.label: The 5 Best Songs Of The Week, Oct 23

items.title: Death Keeps Me Alive
items.note: The lead single from a metal-inspired album, taking the tumult of "Wasted Days" and giving it a metallic edge, showing renewed ferociousness.

items.title: Where Is Gone?
items.note: Big topic in the music meeting; Tumelo called it intense, mature, and heavy-hitting. Fontaines' new album DOPAMINE CHAMBER came out that Friday.

items.title: Goblin's Head
items.note: Listed as the first track in the New Music Discovery playlist for 23 October 2026.

items.title: HOWDYPARTNER
items.note: Featured on the weekly playlist of brand new music from under-the-radar artists.

items.title: Northside Needs Me
items.note: Featured on the weekly playlist of brand new music from under-the-radar artists.

items.title: He Keeps Talking
items.note: Latest single from the album Dance Tunes for the End of the World; barrels toward apocalypse while embracing entropy, sounding sincere rather than ironic.

items.title: Haunted Castles
items.note: Opening single from The Tide, starting reflective before building into something urgent and cathartic, with real drums and bigger guitars.

items.title: Old Home Video
items.note: Written while their mother had dementia; mixes grief in anticipation of loss with fondness and sorrow, described as the most unguarded track on Death Drive.

items.title: Shōmetsu / Kodō
items.note: Over eight-minute single moving from a mournful piano piece into cataclysmic doom metal, featuring several guest musicians.

items.title: Mayahuel
items.note: Hypnotic, low-tempo cumbia rebajada drawing on Mexica mythology, with a video directed by Barajas herself.

items.title: Full Powers
items.note: Single from the album 21 Bum Salute, swinging between swaggering confidence and something volatile, with a video made with help from John-Henry Pajak and Jos Eastwood.

items.title: I Will Not Apologize For What I Am
items.note: Album opener built on a plaintive melody played on somber keys, described as genuinely heartbreaking.

items.title: Tobuza Buzibwa
items.note: Kampala MC spitting verses with militant defiance over the track.

items.title: Commodore
items.note: Sydney artist's contribution to the mutant gqom collision of Los Angeles, Durban, and Sydney sounds.
